video_title: 🧸 I Love My New Toy! (🐘 Elephant & 🐷 Piggie #5)

summaries.summary: A friend asks Piggy what he is doing. Piggy shows a new toy and says he loves it, but he does not know what it does. The friend thinks it may be a throwing toy and asks to try it. Piggy throws it with a zip, and the friend throws it back with a zoom. The toy breaks. Piggy becomes mad because his new toy is broken. The friend says, “I am sorry.” Soon, Piggy says he does not care and shows the friend a break and snap toy. They play by saying, “Break! Snap!” Then Piggy asks if the friend wants to play with his new toy. The friend says no and explains, “I want to play with you. Friends are more fun than toys.” The friend says, “You’re it!” Piggy says, “No. You are the end.”

video_title: Going Places - Sesame Street - Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Big Bird's airplane flies high in the sky, and the town below looks tiny. Betty Lou drives an ambulance to the hospital while its red light flashes a warning. Cookie Monster's train chugs along as a car and a bus wait at the crossing. A fire truck's siren shrieks, so everyone gets out of the way. Honk honk! Telly Monster rides his shiny new bicycle and delivers newspapers to everyone on Sesame Street. Prairie Dawn drives a fast police car, catches a speeder, and writes a ticket. Bert's fairy boat carries people in cars back and forth all day. Rodeo Rosy's jeep bounces over the sandy range, past the cows. Ernie's tugboat pushes a big ocean liner into port. Tot's blimp glides over the city, and everyone waves. Harry Monster drives the Sesame Street bus up town, downtown, across town, and around town, taking people where they want to go. At the last stop, everybody gets off.

Nate the Great is a detective who works alone. After eating pancakes, he gets a call from Annie. She lost a yellow picture of her dog, Fang. Nate goes to her house and searches her yellow room, but the picture is not there. He watches Fang bury a bone, so he and Annie dig in the yard. They find no picture. Next, Nate talks to Rosamond, who has four cats. While leaving, he finds her lost cat, Super Hex, under his chair. Then Nate meets Annie’s brother, Harry, who paints him red. Nate looks at Harry’s paintings and notices that one monster is orange. He understands that Harry painted the red monster over Annie’s yellow picture of Fang. The yellow and red paint mixed together. The dog’s ears and tail became the monster’s three heads. Annie is upset, but she plans to paint a new picture. Nate eats pancakes, says goodbye, and walks home in the rain, glad he is wearing his rubbers.

Amelia Bedelia goes to school because Mrs. Rogers asks her to tell Mr. Carter that the school telephone is broken. Mr. Carter is glad to see her because the children are wild, so he leaves her with Miss Lane’s list of lessons. Amelia Bedelia takes every instruction literally. She rolls when the list says “call the roll,” sings one song, and makes the children run when reading says “run, run, run.” She buys bulbs for their science lesson, even though the closet has only onions. During quiet reading, she thinks the children should read aloud. For art, she tells them to find pictures to paint, so they take pictures from the walls. She turns play practice into playing and makes math problems with real apples. The children chase one another to take away apples. Amelia Bedelia cooks the apples into toffee apples. Mrs. Rogers returns with the real new teacher, Miss Reid. The children have already gone home, but everyone eats toffee apples, and Miss Reid says Amelia Bedelia may teach again.

video_title: Nate the Great Goes Undercover (Nate the Great)

summaries.summary: Nate the Great is a detective. His neighbor Oliver asks him to find who tips over his garbage can every night. After breakfast, Nate and his dog, Sludge, ask Rosamond and Esmeralda questions, but neither they nor their animals took the garbage. Nate decides that an animal or bird must be doing it. He reads about night animals at the library. That night, Nate hides near the garbage can, then searches outside. In a field, he finds a skunk beside some garbage. The skunk sprays him, so Nate thinks the case is solved. He tells Oliver to use mothballs, but the garbage can is tipped over again. Nate hides inside the can to find proof. Sludge comes, knocks off the cover, and looks inside. Nate discovers that Sludge is the garbage snatcher. Sludge was hungry and wanted a snack. Nate gives him dog food and a bone. Then Nate rests, tired from his first night case.

Nate the Great is on vacation with his dog, Sludge, when his friend Claude asks for help finding a lost grocery list. Claude remembers salt, milk, butter, flour, sugar, tuna fish, eggs, and baking powder, but he does not remember where he lost it. Nate draws a map and follows the streets with Claude and Sludge. The wind blows the map toward Rosamond’s house. There, Rosamond is making fishy cat pancakes from a paper she found. Outside, Fang holds another paper, but it is Nate’s map. Nate makes Sludge bark, so Fang drops the paper. Nate catches it, but learns it is not the list. At home, Nate makes pancakes and realizes that Rosamond’s recipe uses the same foods as Claude’s list. He returns to Rosamond’s house and discovers that her recipe is the lost grocery list. Nate gives it back to Claude, then goes home to finish his vacation.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Rot: The Cutest in the WORLD!

summaries.summary: Rot is a mutant baked potato who loves mud, garbage-can food, checkers, and games. When he sees a sign for the “cutest in the world” contest, he decides to enter and sings, “I’m the cutest in the world.” At the contest, Rot sees a baby, a cuddly kitten, pink puppies, and jolly jellyfish. The other contestants do not think Rot can win. Rot thinks about eating them all, but decides that would cause indigestion. He tries to look cuter by wearing big ears, whiskers, and pink decorations, but none of these make him feel cute. Rot then decides to be himself. When it is his turn, he goes onstage, smiles his biggest smile, and shows his best side. The judges, a rotten banana and an apple pear, choose Rot as the winner and give him a shiny trophy. Rot looks at his reflection and says, “I’m the cutest in the world!” Then he notices he is wearing a unibrow.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth and her cousin, Ollie!

summaries.summary: Ronan was a mighty barbarian who led his people. He invaded, raided, and traded gold, jewelry, weapons, and tools. One day, he got a book, but no one wanted to trade for it. At home, Ronan thought the book was useless. Then he saw a picture and began to read. He read all night. The next day, his friends found him reading, but they told him barbarians should raid. Ronan went raiding, yet he could not stop thinking about the book. He read it to the end and began taking books during every raid. Soon, his boat was full of books. Ronan built a library, but his friends did not want to read. To show them what books could do, he read aloud about Odin and the kraken. The barbarians became interested and filled the library. Ronan made library rules, gave out cards, recommended books, and read to the younglings. Ronan became a mighty librarian, and his people invaded, raided, and read.

video_title: 🇺🇸 I Am Martin Luther King, Jr—Kids Book MLK Day Black History Month Read Aloud Story

summaries.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. dreamed that Black and white children could join hands as brothers and sisters and that freedom would ring. After the March on Washington, the president and Congress passed civil rights laws, but the work was not finished. In Selma, Alabama, 600 activists began walking fifty-four miles to Montgomery to demand voting rights because rules stopped Black people from voting. Police used billy clubs and tear gas and stopped the peaceful marchers. The group tried again with 2,500 people, but they were stopped again. On March 21, 1965, 8,000 people marched. Black and white Christians and Jewish people joined them. They marched for two days through rain and exhaustion. President Johnson sent troops to protect them, and they reached Montgomery with tears of joy. King said to answer hate with love and violence with kindness. Funtown later opened to Black people. King won the Nobel Peace Prize, fought poverty, and is remembered on a national holiday. He stood for peace, justice, and helping others.

video_title: Follow the Drinking Gourd by Jeanette Winter read aloud

summaries.summary: Long ago, Peg Leg Joe helped enslaved people escape. He worked on cotton plantations and taught them a secret song about following the drinking gourd, using the stars and trail signs to find freedom. When Molly’s husband, James, was sold away, they took their son Isaiah, Old Hattie, and young George and escaped that night. They walked by night and hid by day, avoiding slave catchers and hungry animals. They followed rivers, dead trees, and the stars. A farm boy shared bacon and cornbread with them. At the river’s end, Peg Leg Joe carried them across the wide Ohio River. Farmers then guided the five travelers along the Underground Railroad. They hid in a barn and later rested in a secret room at a Quaker farm. They traveled by foot and cart to Lake Erie. Finally, they boarded a steamship to Canada. Old Hattie said five more souls were safe when they reached freedom.
